heckles.message: Skin locked per map, heart and strip landmarks, city towers scale with district size
heckles.heckle:
A hundred and forty six lines added to one index.html, because apparently the intern thinks a file is a landfill. You deleted the Skin button from the top bar and then bolted a new #scount button rule on, so the layout shuffles like a cabinet after a filibuster. Skins locked per map means the player loses a choice, and the commit message promises heart and strip landmarks like a campaign pledge with no budget. City towers scaling with district size is more math buried in the same giant script with no tests.

Fix it: Split the skin CSS and the map logic out of index.html into separate files. Check that the #scount button rule does not squeeze the top bar on a narrow phone. Tell the player why the skin is locked instead of silently removing the Skin button. Write one test for tower scaling.

heckles.message: West and Bunker skins, Meadow fields with scoring and Biggest Meadow record
heckles.heckle:
Three hundred and thirty five lines in one commit. West skin, Bunker skin, Meadow scoring, and a record, all dumped in index.html like a bailout bill with forty riders nobody read. The body.ww block is a wall of one line CSS with hardcoded browns and a Georgia font stack, copied from the War skin with the colors swapped, which is what an intern does when the deadline is in five minutes. The Meadow scoring and the record sit in the same inline script as everything else, so one typo takes the whole game down.

Fix it: Move the skin palettes into CSS variables instead of cloning whole body.ww and body.w blocks. Pull Meadow scoring out of the giant inline script. Guard the Biggest Meadow record against bad localStorage data. Ship one feature per commit.

heckles.message: War skin: army map with trenches, bases, HQs and marching soldiers
heckles.heckle:
A War skin with trenches, bases, HQs and marching soldiers, all in the same index.html that is already groaning. The new body.w block is a pile of hardcoded olive and khaki hex colors with a Courier New font, copy pasted from the other skins with the paint changed. Marching soldiers means a new animation loop, and I see no sign anyone checked what it does to a phone battery. Your skin system is now a heap of body letters like w, c and ww, which reads like a ransom note.

Fix it: Give the skin classes real names instead of w, c and ww in index.html. Share one skin template and override only the colors. Cap the soldier animation frame rate and pause it when the tab is hidden. Stop growing a single file past the point of sanity.

Another steward pull request, another one line minified JSON blob in contrib/steward, merged with a button click like a rubber stamp. The payload is a place_hatch call for a crosswalk on a street, with six digit coordinates and a hatch spacing of 610. Nobody can review a single minified line, and the merge is the only quality gate, which is government efficiency at its finest. The bot cannot even keep its timestamp name consistent without human cleanup.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib/steward JSON so a diff means something. Add a schema check that rejects a bad place_hatch call before merge. Stop merging these by hand and let a workflow validate and merge them.

heckles.message: Add Teardown tab, merge Pipeline Builder in as Builder tab
heckles.heckle:
Seven hundred and forty nine lines into index.html for a Teardown tab with sixty one hand typed products, and a Pipeline Builder smashed in as a tab, like merging two failing departments and calling it reform. The second style block is a late patch tacked on after the first one, with fresh pb and td classes beside the comic skin rules. The changelog line is one giant paragraph that nobody will read. Every layer is marked known or inferred, which is a polite way of admitting you are guessing.

Fix it: Move the sixty one product records out of index.html into a data file. Fold the second style block into the main stylesheet. Cut the CHANGELOG.md entry down to two sentences. Check the new tabs on a small phone.

The grok bot pushed straight to the branch again with no pull request, no review and no gate, like a senator voting on a bill he never read. The file contrib/grok/2026-11-19T172357.json is one minified line of place_line calls with negative coordinates for a Mesquite House wall, plus door checks stuffed into meta arrays. Nothing proves the walls close or the door checks pass. A direct push under the developer login means the history cannot tell the bot from the intern.

Fix it: Make the grok bot open a pull request like the other bots. Validate the door height and door width checks in the JSON before it lands. Format the file so a human can read it. Give the bot its own commit author.

heckles.message: Per pipe and shifting line colors
heckles.heckle:
Per pipe and shifting colors, in a single index.html, with a new inkMode global and a pipeInk function that returns a raw hsl string rebuilt on every call. The strokeEdgeShift function breaks an edge into six point chunks inside a loop, so the draw path does string building per segment like it is paying by the allocation. Three modes named all, pipe and shift live in loose var globals with matching display names in another object, so adding a fourth means editing three places. Nice little rainbow, intern, shame about the plumbing.

Fix it: Cache the hsl strings in pipeInk in index.html instead of rebuilding them per segment. Put the ink modes in one table. Check that p.ink and p.hue exist for old saved pipes. Test shifting mode on a long pipe for frame drops.

heckles.message: Full screen button
heckles.heckle:
A Full screen button, wired by hand with a fixed position hack, in a file that already has too many buttons. The new #fsBtn sits absolute at the bottom right with a z-index of 5 and fades to 0.55 opacity in full screen, so it hovers over the canvas right where a thumb will draw. The body.fs rule hides the bar and status pill, so once you are in there the only way out is the ghost button. There is no sign of a real fullscreen API fallback for phones that refuse it.

Fix it: Check that requestFullscreen actually exists in index.html and fall back gracefully on iPhones. Move #fsBtn away from the drawing area. Give the player an obvious exit that is not a faded button.

heckles.message: High scores: post each shift to the Score Hub, per task boards in the review and the menu
heckles.heckle:
Fifty five lines added to just-five-more-v1.html so the game can post scores to a public hub, and I see the board styles stacked right on top of the math styles like laundry on a chair. A three letter name input with text-transform uppercase is the only identity check, so anyone can post anything. The fixed height 150px board will clip on a small phone, and the grid of two buttons with 12px text is cramped. Posting every shift to a hub with no proof the score is real is a rigged election with extra steps.

Fix it: Validate the score on the server in the hub instead of trusting the client in just-five-more-v1.html. Let the board height flex on small screens. Handle a failed post with a visible retry. Debounce the post button so one shift cannot spam the hub.

heckles.message: Connector tiles for every edge combination and auto hole filling
heckles.heckle:
An IIFE that brute forces every four edge combination out of the letters C, R, F and W with four nested loops, then pushes filler tiles into DEFS at load time. It is clever in the way a lit match in a barn is clever. The weights are a magic .12 and the lake flag is a one line ternary nobody can read. Every page load now burns cycles building tiles that could be a static list. The nested loops use a, b, c and e as variable names, because apparently d was taken and imagination was not.

Fix it: Name the loop variables and the .12 weight in index.html. Build the connector list once and check it in instead of generating it on load. Add a test that no edge pattern is missing. Explain the lake rule in a comment.

heckles.message: Highways, roundabouts, intersections, fabric weaves, stair presets and skin, picture stamps, radiant pop and under the sea themes, fish, fill canvas
heckles.heckle:
One commit, 171 lines added to a single index.html, and it ships fourteen picture stamps, eleven new pattern styles, two fill buttons and a new rules hint paragraph like a bailout bill with every rider the committee could staple on. The stampSel dropdown hardcodes fourteen options in markup while the drawing for each lives somewhere else, so adding a fifteenth means editing two places, which is how an intern builds a filibuster. The pattern select is now a wall of twenty something options on a phone screen. The commit message is a grocery list, because you could not decide what the commit was about, and neither could I. Did you learn version control from the back of a cereal box?

Fix it: Split this into one commit per feature so the history is readable. Build the stamp options from a single stamps object in index.html instead of hand typing the select. Group the pattern select with optgroups so mobile users can find anything. Move the rules hint text out of the markup into data.

heckles.message: City skin redrawn as detailed illustrations with cached tile art and lit 3D buildings
heckles.heckle:
You redrew the whole City skin and managed to touch 220 lines of a single index.html, rewriting every body.c selector like a campaign promise nobody asked for. Swapping blue and yellow for beige and teal is a paint job on a file that still holds every skin as hand pasted CSS blocks, so the next skin means another stack of body.x lines. The message claims cached tile art and lit 3D buildings, yet the diff is mostly color values, so either the message lies or the real work is buried where nobody can review it. Hex codes repeated forty times with no variables is how you get a government shutdown in stylesheet form. I have seen interns with more discipline and less caffeine.

Fix it: Define the skin colors as CSS custom properties in index.html and reference them from the body.c rules. Split the cache and building drawing into its own commit. Move SKINS and the skin CSS out of the single file. Write a commit message that matches the diff.

heckles.message: City skin with 3D towers in iso, full River tile set, skin-aware names
heckles.heckle:
Two hundred lines landing in a single index.html, and the new City skin is a pile of body.c selectors bolted onto a file that already had body.g, body.k and whatever else you stapled on last week. Skins as copy pasted CSS blocks is a zoning board approving every shack that shows up with a form. Light grey and blue also means the dark themes that rescued your eyes are now optional, which is how you get a game that looks like a tax portal. Iso towers drawn inline in the same file means one typo and the whole map goes down, and you ship with no tests like a campaign promise ships with no plan.

Fix it: Move each skin into a data object instead of a new body class in index.html. Split the drawing code out of the page into its own script file. Check the City skin on a phone width, because the bottom bar is cramped. Add one smoke test that loads every skin.

heckles.message: Circuit style with AC and DC boards, schematic parts and legend; Cyber, Color Pop and Escher Remix skins with new tile patterns
heckles.heckle:
Four new skins and a circuit style in one commit, all dumped into the same index.html like a spending bill with nine riders nobody read. The .cp-body, .cp-line and .cp-hot classes are hardcoded hex colors, #24382c and #ff7a00 sprayed everywhere instead of the CSS variables you already defined, so the skins you just added cannot even be themed. The .ps-power .valve-arrow selector got patched with a comma instead of a real rule, which is duct tape on a bailout. Pretty sure the intern thinks a commit is a place to hide things.

Fix it: Replace the hardcoded hex values in the .cp-* rules in index.html with the existing CSS variables. Split the circuit, cyber and Escher skins into separate commits next time. Pull the SVG part builders out of the one giant file. Test the legend on a narrow phone screen.

heckles.message: Synth sounds with mute button, one way check valves, vault difficulty levels; shuffled vault chips; no stale clear cards after leaving Pipes
heckles.heckle:
This commit is five features and a bug fix wearing a trench coat. Synth sounds, a mute button, check valves, vault difficulty and a stale card fix all landed together in index.html, so if any one breaks you get to bisect a sandwich. The new .sound-btn has a 36 pixel hit area jammed next to the hamburger in .top-left with a 4 pixel gap, which on a phone is a fat finger lottery. Audio that starts with no mute memory is also how you get yelled at on a bus. The stale clear card fix tells me you knew the state handling was shaky and shipped anyway.

Fix it: Store the mute choice in localStorage so it survives a reload. Widen the gap between .menu-btn and .sound-btn in index.html. One feature per commit from here on. Add a guard that resets card state whenever the mode changes, not only when leaving Pipes.

heckles.message: Tile Spinner Vault accepts difficulty-scaled scores up to 3000
heckles.heckle:
You raised the vault max from 1000 to 3000 and doubled perSecond to 200 in api/_games.js, which is a cheat code with a changelog. Anyone who can hit the score endpoint can now post a 3000 in two seconds and sit atop the board like a lobbyist at a committee hearing. The perSecond limit is the only thing guarding the leaderboard, and you loosened it because your own client got rejected. That is fixing the referee instead of the game. Also this is the third changelog line for a single afternoon, in a file full of v2026.11.18b and c, which reads like a filibuster in version numbers.

Fix it: Validate the difficulty multiplier on the server in api/_games.js instead of just raising max. Tie perSecond to the difficulty so Easy cannot post an Expert score. Merge the same day changelog entries in CHANGELOG.md into one.

heckles.message: Pipe styles (classic, water mains, streets, power lines) and Big boards in three sizes; hide vault panel outside Play
heckles.heckle:
Pipe styles and three Big board sizes in one shot, and the CSS grew pole, house, house-lit and pseg classes with colors sprinkled in as raw hex like #7a5a3a and #ffd23a. The .ps-streets, .ps-power and .ps-water pipe-base overrides are three copies of the same rule with different paint, the kind of cloning that gets a department defunded. The statA line now checks P.big in a ternary inside the render function, so every mode keeps getting one more special case welded onto the same if chain. That chain is a tax code at this point.

Fix it: Collapse the three .ps-* pipe-base rules in index.html into one rule driven by CSS variables. Replace the mode if chain in the stats render with a lookup table. Keep the new hex colors in one palette block. Check the Big boards on a small phone.

heckles.message: Vault: blank ring on every junction, five hide digits, the rest are decoys
heckles.heckle:
A blank ring on every junction and most of them decoys. Congratulations, you built a game where the main mechanic is clicking on nothing. The hint text now literally says most rings are empty decoys, which is you admitting the design needs an apology on screen. The vault-ring rule gained a transition on fill, stroke and opacity all at once, on every ring on a big board, which is a nice way to make a cheap phone cry. And the dashed .vault-spot.empty rings at 0.45 opacity will be nearly invisible outside, so players will be tapping fog.

Fix it: Drop the transition on stroke and opacity in .vault-ring in index.html for large boards. Raise the contrast of .vault-spot.empty so decoys are readable in sunlight. Rewrite the hint text so it explains the goal instead of confessing the design.

heckles.message: Post Rush, Pipes and Vault scores to the score hub; tap outside a card to close it
heckles.heckle:
You wired score posting into the game card with a three letter tag input, which means the entire leaderboard identity system is a text box and a prayer. No auth, no rate limit on the client, and a shared hub that now trusts whatever the page sends it. The .post-tag field is 76 pixels wide with letter spacing of 0.2em, which on a phone will clip a three letter tag like a cheap suit. Tap outside a card to close it also means a stray thumb during a score entry throws the whole run away. Nice touch for the intern who loves lost data.

Fix it: Do not close the card in the index.html tap handler while the .post-tag input has focus or text. Add a client side cooldown on the score post. Widen .post-tag so the letters are not clipped. Make the server in the score hub reject empty tags.

heckles.message: Register Tile Spinner rush, pipes and vault boards
heckles.heckle:
Three new boards stuffed into api/_games.js, and look at the numbers you made up. Rush max 500 at one per second, vault max 1000 at 100 per second, pipes max 100000 over 400 days. Those limits are guesses with decimal places missing, like a budget projection written on a napkin. The vault one was wrong within the hour, since the very next commit had to raise it, so you shipped a config you never tested against your own game. The changelog entry labelled v2026.11.18b also skips a plain v2026.11.18 on the same day, a version scheme invented while falling down stairs.

Fix it: Play each board once and set max and perSecond from real runs in api/_games.js. Write the vault limit with its difficulty multiplier from the start. Fix the version label in CHANGELOG.md so it is not a b with no a.

heckles.message: Vault digits sit on the real yellow match dots; pips track real match progress; near-match hint glow
heckles.heckle:
So the vault digits were NOT sitting on the real match dots until now. That means the previous vault commit shipped a puzzle whose answers were in the wrong place, and you are patching a bug the same afternoon like an agency issuing a correction to its own press release. The new vertexProgress function has a hex branch, a square branch and a pile of special cases in the same index.html, and it calls tileMap.get with a template string key for every vertex on every render, which is a garbage collector protest waiting to happen. Fifty one lines deleted and ninety added to move dots, and not one test.

Fix it: Cache the tileMap key strings in vertexProgress in index.html instead of rebuilding them every render. Put the hex and square branches into separate small functions. Add a test that the vault digits land on lit match vertices for every grid type.

heckles.message: Completion chimes, record celebration, player outlines, bot opponents
heckles.heckle:
Bot opponents, chimes, outlines and a record celebration in one commit to index.html, and the bot logic landed in a file that also holds the rules text as raw HTML. You even jammed two paragraphs on one line with a stray closing p tag like a rider on a defense bill. The how to play text now says bots take their turns on their own, with zero word on how smart they are, because the answer is probably a random number generator wearing a tie. A chime per tile rising in pitch means a ten tile castle sounds like an ice cream truck having a stroke, and there is no mention of a volume control or mute anywhere.

Fix it: Add a mute toggle for the chimes in index.html. Split the two rules paragraphs onto separate lines. Add a bot turn delay setting so players can follow what it did. Move the bot code out of the page file.

Another day, another robot dumps a one line JSON file into contrib/agent-orange and you merge it like a senator signing a bill he never read. This one claims a chunk, declares the same port value of 5486 on all four edges like a copy paste campaign promise, then defines an agricultural lot with a single minified line nobody on earth can review. A pull request with no reviewer, no tests and no description is a rubber stamp with extra steps, and you are the stamp.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib/agent-orange JSON so a diff means something. Add a validator step that rejects duplicate port values on every edge of a chunk. Make the merge check the file against the chunk it claims before it lands.

The grok bot pushed straight to the branch under your name again, no pull request, no gate, no adult supervision, like a executive order nobody voted on. Its contrib/grok file builds a cottage out of place_line calls with negative coordinates, a wall height of 3658 repeated per segment, and door checks buried in the meta of one wall. All of it is crammed on a single line, so the intern who approved this setup could not find a bug in it with a flashlight.

Fix it: Make grok open pull requests like the other bots instead of pushing to the branch. Put the wall height once per building rather than on every line segment. Move the door checks out of wall meta into their own call. Format contrib/grok files so a human can read them.

This merge removes two ids, 36638 and 36637, then plants a sign symbol whose text is a whole calendar essay about orbits, hectodays and farm season. Stuffing paragraphs of lore into meta.text on a sign is how you build a bloated map that loads like a government website. The remove calls fire by raw numeric id with nothing proving those ids still belong to the thing the bot meant, which is a bailout with no audit.

Fix it: Verify remove ids against the object type and owner before they delete anything in contrib/agent-orange. Cap the length of meta.text on place_symbol calls. Store the calendar text once in data and let the sign point at it.

heckles.message: campus: education genres (history, disasters, safety and more), profiles, course embed fallback, creator seal
heckles.heckle:
You cloned your own YouTube backend, renamed the header comment, and shipped 682 lines of index.js like a filibuster that finally ran out of speakers. Every route in there, /sources/remove, /sources/genre, /entry, /clip, is wide open behind app.use(cors()) with no auth at all, so any stranger can delete your course list from a browser console. The database is sql.js rewriting the entire file with fs.writeFileSync on every change, which is a bailout plan for a problem you invented. The .gitignore lists *.db twice, which tells me nobody read it, least of all the intern who wrote it. And package.json still says name backend with an empty description and a test script that just errors out.

Fix it: Put a shared secret check in front of the write routes in index.js. Lock cors() down to the campus origin. Debounce the writeFileSync save in index.js or move to a real database. Delete the duplicate *.db line in .gitignore. Give package.json a real name and description.

heckles.message: campus: education genres (history, disasters, safety and more), profiles, course embed fallback, creator seal
heckles.heckle:
A single index.html with 934 added lines, all the CSS, all the markup and all the script crammed into one file like a omnibus spending bill nobody read. The viewport meta has user-scalable=no, so anyone with bad eyes gets zero zoom, nice work. The body is overflow hidden with every screen absolutely positioned and scrolling on its own, which is a coin flip on small phones. API_BASE is hardcoded to a Railway URL in the client, and the page loads the YouTube iframe_api from a CDN with no failure path I can see. Profiles live in a getProfile() call and get shoved into query strings, so identity is whatever the intern types. The commit message promises a creator seal and I can barely find it in this wall of text.

Fix it: Remove user-scalable=no from the viewport meta in index.html. Split the inline style and script into separate files. Move API_BASE into one config spot. Add an error state for when the iframe_api fails to load. Stop sending the profile name as a bare query string to /transcript.

heckles.message: trigger production build from GitHub
heckles.heckle:
An empty commit to poke Vercel, because apparently the intern's deploy pipeline needs a nudge like a stalled bill needs a lobbyist. No files, no change, no explanation beyond the message, and I get to read it anyway. If your first push needs a manual kick every single time, the problem is the Vercel project link, not the git log.

Fix it: Check the Vercel project Git connection for this repo. Stop spamming empty commits into the history of 2026-11-17-orange-campus.

heckles.message: Register Raineurysm Puzzle on the score hub
heckles.heckle:
One line added to api/_games.js and you wrapped it in two changelog edits and a README rewrite, like holding a press conference to announce a parking ticket. The entry for raineurysm-puzzle sets max 60000 and perSecond 300, numbers pulled out of thin air with no comment explaining them, while every other game gets a note about its format. The maxMs of 30 days is a hand pasted line copied from mill-ionaire with the arithmetic changed. The registry is a hand pasted list that grows one copy paste at a time, and it will rot exactly like every other hand pasted list you own.

Fix it: Add a comment in api/_games.js saying where 60000 and 300 came from. Replace the copy pasted entries with a shared defaults object. Trim the CHANGELOG.md entry so it does not repeat the README.

heckles.message: Neighborhood preset: curvy main streets with straight side streets
heckles.heckle:
A preset called Neighborhood landed in index.html, and the way you got there was editing a hint paragraph by one word, adding the word straight to a wall of text nobody reads. That hint paragraph is a single giant line of prose jammed in a p tag like a campaign promise with no budget behind it. The select now has Nautilus, Willow, Crystal, Neighborhood, Your pattern and Custom, a menu that reads like the intern named things as they came to mind. The preset logic itself is stuffed into the same one file as everything else in this toy, so every tweak makes the diff harder to read than the last.

Fix it: Break the steps hint paragraph in index.html into short separate lines. Move the preset definitions out of index.html into their own small file. Put the preset options in a sensible order in the select.

heckles.message: Detailer key v1: per-agent Anthropic key for the detailer, Railway login and DNS fix built in
heckles.heckle:
You committed blue-agent-detailer-key-v1.sh, a shell script that makes you paste a secret key into a phone terminal, which is how a toddler would run key rotation if toddlers had root. The only validation is a case statement checking the prefix, so any typo with the right first letters sails through to production like a bailout with no strings. Then you print the last four characters of the key to the console for fun. The repo is a junk drawer of one shot scripts with versions baked into filenames. The set -e plus the pull and the deploy in one blob means a half failed run leaves the service in a mystery state.

Fix it: Stop shipping one shot scripts in the repo root and keep one parameterized setup script. Check the key length and charset in blue-agent-detailer-key-v1.sh, not just the prefix. Quit echoing any part of the key. Add a trap so a failed deploy says what state the service is in. Delete the filename version suffix and let git do its job.

heckles.message: Hidden growth dots during play, scaled cars and critters, 30 plus presets, new steps, rule switching, surprise me
heckles.heckle:
One commit that hides dots, scales cars and critters, adds thirty presets, new steps, rule switching and a Surprise me button. That is not a commit, that is an omnibus spending bill with a rider for every senator. All of it landed as 124 added lines in one index.html that was already a single file wall of canvas code, so good luck finding anything when the pinch bug returns. The bEdit toggle sits next to Save image, Clear and Zoom in a row that was cramped on a phone before you added a fourth button. And a button labeled Edit dots: On that is hidden during play is a label that lies half the time.

Fix it: Split this into five commits, one per feature. Move the preset tables out of index.html into their own file. Check the toolbar row around bEdit and bSurprise at phone width and let it wrap. Make the bEdit label match what is actually visible during play. Give Surprise me a seed so a bad result can be reproduced.

heckles.message: Clean single shape sides in isometric, open space under bridges
heckles.heckle:
A fix titled clean single shape sides, which is a polite way of saying the last commit drew the sides wrong and nobody noticed until you looked at it. In drawIsoBody you stuffed bo, BL and BR into the same comma chain of var declarations until the line reads like a ransom note, and the function now hauls around GL, GR, BL and BR with names a single letter apart. One typo swapping L and R and your bridges render inside out, and nothing here would tell you. Sixteen lines added and fifteen removed with no test, no screenshot, no nothing, just vibes and a prayer.

Fix it: Break the var chain in drawIsoBody in index.html into named objects so left and right cannot be swapped quietly. Rename GL, GR, BL and BR to something a human can read. Add a tiny render check for the bridge case. Stop patching the isometric view one tweak per commit and batch your fixes.

heckles.message: Tabbed interface, isometric view, bridges and tunnels at crossings
heckles.heckle:
You bolted a tabbed interface, a whole isometric renderer, bridges and tunnels onto a pipe toy in one commit, 152 lines added to a single index.html, like a campaign promise to fix healthcare, infrastructure and the weather before lunch. The #bar rule got rewritten with padding stacked on safe area math, so every tab you added eats vertical space from the canvas on a phone, which already had overflow hidden and no way to scroll when the bar gets tall. Bridges and tunnels at crossings means every crossing now needs depth logic, and the intern did it inside the draw path with no separate module, so every frame pays for it.

Fix it: Pull the isometric code out of index.html into its own script file. Cap the height of #bar and let the tab content scroll inside it. Cache the crossing detection instead of recomputing it each frame. Test the tabs on a small phone in landscape before you push again.

heckles.message: MobbyHill vehicle unlocks in the token wallet
heckles.heckle:
Two lines in a changelog, one more line in a README, and a price table crammed into api/_wallets.js as a single run on line of part names that now scrolls off the screen like a filibuster. Every new item you add means editing the same unreadable line, and one missed comma takes the whole wallet down for every game on the hub. The prices live in this file and again in the game itself, so the day you change one and forget the other, players see 1500 and get charged something else. You also hand wrote a version tag with a letter suffix, d, which tells me the previous three were not enough to teach you anything.

Fix it: Put one item per line in api/_wallets.js so a diff shows what changed. Make the game read prices from the hub instead of keeping a second copy. Add a check that every price in the game exists in the wallet file. Generate the changelog tag instead of typing it.

heckles.message: Token unlocks for the side by side, SUV and pickup
heckles.heckle:
You locked three vehicles behind tokens by pasting a VEHPRICE object into index.html, which is the client, which the player owns. The unlock state lives in localStorage next to the options, so anyone with a console can hand themselves a pickup for free, and the price list in the page is a suggestion, not a rule. Your own comment admits the spending goes through the score hub wallet, so the server holds the truth and the page holds a polite fiction. Then you added an unlock dialog with a Not now button to a start menu that was already four sections tall on a phone. Congress passes cleaner paywalls.

Fix it: Check ownership on the server wallet before a locked vehicle is allowed to start a scored run in index.html. Never trust the unlock flag read back from localStorage. Check the unl panel and the vehicle row at phone width and make sure Unlock is reachable without scrolling. Move VEHPRICE out of the page so the hub is the only source of prices.

heckles.message: Creator seal with donate pill
heckles.heckle:
A donate pill pasted straight into pajamastan index.html, 30 lines of seal markup and css hand copied from the creator-seal file, because apparently importing a file is for people with real jobs. heckles.message: Music mode top down: place beat objects on matching ground, cars follow streets
heckles.heckle:
The buildSurf function in cityseek-music-v1.js redraws the entire city onto a canvas one sixth the size, then reads every pixel back and guesses what surface it is by nearest color distance against six hard coded RGB triples in GROUND. That is not a ground map, that is a guess dressed up as a map, and any palette tweak turns every car into a tree. The try and catch wrapped around all of it swallows every error and sets surf to null, so when it breaks it breaks silently, the way a bad budget does. getImageData on a large canvas will also stall a phone.

Fix it: Ask the city generator for road and grass data instead of reverse engineering it from pixels in buildSurf. Log the error in that catch instead of eating it. Build the map once and cache it per city code. Test with the Muted look, since GROUND only matches the Bold colors.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: engine with zoom reveal and tower floors
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: spy hunt v2

heckles.message: Add LANGUAGES tab: spoken words, ancient numerals and world digit scripts

heckles.message: Backup orbit feed when CelesTrak refuses, skip bad orbit records

heckles.message: Composite: pick which roadside things to cut out from everything the current model knows

heckles.message: Road tracking: lock onto your own lane on multi lane roads and map the other lane lines
heckles.heckle:
You wrote a lane detector in a single index.html, and the peak finder is a quadruple nested loop over a 48 by W/4 accumulator, run per frame, on a phone. The non maximum suppression scan checks 7 by 17 neighbors for every cell above threshold, which is O(cells times 119) of pure hope. The magic numbers 0.12, 0.15, 30 and 60 to 120 are scattered like campaign promises, and loosening the tracking penalty from dx/60 to dx/120 just makes the lines jump lanes more easily. Hand tuned thresholds with no test footage in the repo.

heckles.message: Add Road tab: lane line, vanishing point and bend tracking saved per recording
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Add Map tab: coverage routes, spot search and projects

heckles.message: Add stop motion capture by distance or time, alongside or instead of full video
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Save recordings inside the app with a library, crash recovery and battery stop

heckles.message: Solar burst simulator: flare, proton storm, CME impact on magnetosphere; NASA DONKI proxy
